tex_content.html:
\begin{claim} \end{claim}[$\mathcal{X}(T_1)$ has nontrivial $\pi _3$] Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1, every component ${\mathcal X}(T_1)$ surviving after the time in Proposition 3 has nontrivial $\pi _3$. \end{claim}
Proof

\sketch The surgery topology preserves the property that each component group is a free product of finite and infinite cyclic groups. Since $\pi _2({\mathcal X}(T_1))=0$, Claim 4 forces $\pi _1({\mathcal X}(T_1))$ to be finite. Its universal cover is a closed simply connected $3$-manifold, hence a homotopy $3$-sphere by Poincare duality, so $\pi _3({\mathcal X}(T_1))\cong \Zee $.

□
